About AI discoveries in 2025

This selection contains 715 catalog entries dated 1 Jan 2025 to 31 Dec 2025. 715 include structured evidence annotations describing reported tests, the AI contribution and remaining limits. Missing annotations mean those details have not been structured here, not that a study lacks evidence.

Dates follow the catalog publication policy. Coverage is selected and incomplete; entries can overlap or describe several results. Counts do not measure independent discoveries, clinical benefit or worldwide research output. Read the selection and evidence policy or compare catalog coverage by year and field.

31 Dec 2025Not stated in the abstract reviewed

A clinically validated 3D deep learning approach for quantifying vascular invasion in pancreatic cancer.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding / tested result: PAN-VIQ segmented pancreatic tumors and five vessels on CT and quantified three-dimensional vessel encasement. It was trained and internally validated on 2,130 cases, externally validated with accuracy above 90%, and prospectively tested in 202 patients; it outperformed junior radiologists and matched senior radiologists in reported accuracy and recall.

Technology: PAN-VIQ deep-learning framework for CT tumor/vessel segmentation and 3D vascular-involvement quantification.

Editorial relevance 53 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
PAN-VIQ deep-learning framework for CT tumor/vessel segmentation and 3D vascular-involvement quantification.
Limitation / still unknown
The prospective cohort supports assessment performance, not improved surgical outcomes or patient benefit.

A multi-objective optimization framework integrating ICSL deep learning for forecasting and scheduling emergency medical supply demand in public health emergencies.

Finding: The open Nature article's Methods and Results establish an ICSL deep-learning demand forecast tied to Wuhan emergency-supply data and a multi-objective scheduling model; the reported improvements are benchmarked against LSTM and BP baselines.

Technology: ICSL combines IVMD, PCR, CNN and LSTM components to forecast emergency-supply demand.

Test and result

Limitation / still unknown

30 Dec 2025Leiden University Medical Center; Amsterdam UMC

A coronary CT model retains diagnostic discrimination in sex subgroups

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A post-hoc analysis tested an existing coronary CT ischemia model against invasive pressure measurements in two cohorts. Vessel-level AUCs in women and men were 0.85 and 0.87 in CREDENCE and 0.81 and 0.86 in PACIFIC-1. These subgroup results do not establish equivalent performance, prospective clinical benefit or a newly developed model.

Technology: Convolutional coronary CT analysis and random-forest ischemia classifier

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Existing neural segmentation/plaque quantification supplied features to a separately trained random forest for vessel-level ischemia prediction.
Test and result
The previously developed classifier used quantitative plaque and stenosis features from neural image analysis; its random forest was trained in a separate 307-patient CREDENCE derivation cohort. This post-hoc study evaluated the 305-patient/868-vessel CREDENCE validation cohort and 208-patient/612-vessel PACIFIC-1 cohort. Sex-specific AUCs exceeded SPECT/MPI comparators; differences from PET in PACIFIC-1 were not significant.
Limitation / still unknown
Vessels are clustered within patients; subgroup tests were post hoc and do not establish equivalence or subgroup fairness. These are reused observational trial cohorts, not four independent samples or a new prospective deployment. Nonsignificant PET differences do not prove equivalence. Clinical outcomes and cost-effectiveness were not tested.

Subclinical Atrial Fibrillation Prediction in Patients with CIED by a Novel Deep Learning Framework.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding / tested result: ResKAN-Attention predicted device-detected subclinical AF in a retrospective cohort of 124 pacemaker patients, with five-fold CV AUC 0.837 and AUC 0.788 in a separately enrolled prospective 35-patient cohort. Editorial relevance 40 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The trained boosting model combined clinical and pathological features into the represented postoperative survival estimates and their cross-cohort prognostic evaluation.
Test and result
The primary Methods retained 4,536 eligible SEER records and split them 3,175:1,361 for training/internal testing. Feature screening and tenfold tuning were described within training. A separate hospital cohort contained 67 women. Overall survival was defined from surgery to all-cause death, with alive patients censored at last follow-up. External GBDT AUCs were reported as 0.839, 0.801 and 0.747 for one-, three- and five-year survival; external differences versus most alternative models were not statistically significant.
Limitation / still unknown
The external cohort is small, retrospective and selected for complete clinical data. Registry treatment timing, exact binary-model handling of censoring and supplementary implementation detail were not independently reconstructed. Model-comparison optimism and transportability remain concerns. Established clinical/pathological predictors are not new biological discoveries. SHAP attribution and observational chemotherapy associations do not establish causal treatment effects; calibration/decision curves are not evidence of actual clinical benefit.

The PROBY deep-learning pipeline screened 26,416 target-validated molecules for useful optical properties, identified 11 candidates for testing and found target-responsive probes PE859 (tau), obatoclax (BCL-2) and B3 (TDP-43).

The first preprint version, posted December 23, 2025, reported two aperiodic and five oscillatory states with marked variation in occupancy, frequency and power across people. Its Methods and Results disagree on whether the cohort contained 64 or 65 participants. A June 2026 revision retained the broad state decomposition but changed numerical frequency estimates; the November 2026 abstract retains the broad finding. These are model-inferred signal patterns, without independent neural-state ground truth, external replication or demonstrated behavioral/clinical meaning.

Technology: Bayesian nonparametric Dirichlet-process Gaussian mixture model with time-delay embedding and stochastic variational inference

Editorial relevance 47 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The DP-GMM clusters time-delay-embedded signal vectors and prunes inactive states, enabling unsupervised group-level decomposition of the MEG data. PSD candidate peaks guided embedding setup and k-NN post-processing was used.
Test and result
A DP-GMM fitted to time-delay-embedded observations was evaluated against thresholding and a time-delay HMM on synthetic signals with known labels, then applied to one left motor-cortex parcel in public resting MEG. Version 1 reported two aperiodic and five oscillatory states, peaks near 9.5/11.5/19.5/22.0/26.5 Hz and median mean lifetimes 0.202–0.263 s; these are historical v1 estimates. Version 3 retained the state-count pattern but revised frequency assignments. V1 Methods says 64 participants while its concatenation account and Results say 65.
Limitation / still unknown
The empirical state labels are inferred by the model and depend on embedding choices, activity selection and post-processing; there is no independent neural-state ground truth or external replication. The original 64/65 cohort discrepancy and later revised state-frequency estimates limit numerical interpretation. No causal link to cognition, disease or clinical outcomes is established.

The journal abstract's three-mechanism count conflicts with a five-reaction claim in the Institute for Protein Design announcement, so the abstract should be treated as authoritative.

Technology: RFdiffusion2

RFdiffusion2 generated scaffolds from atom-level active-site descriptions, LigandMPNN assigned sequences, and structure predictors filtered designs before testing.
Test and result
Designed enzymes were expressed and screened experimentally for retroaldolase, cysteine hydrolase and zinc hydrolase activity, with kinetic constants measured for the best variants.
Limitation / still unknown
Authors state the designs are not as active as native enzymes, the theozymes may miss interactions needed for high activity, and scaffolding catalytic atoms does not guarantee proficient enzymes.

AI-guided subtilisin variants improve aqueous amide formation

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The study reports that wild-type subtilisin BPN′ directly catalyzed condensation of free carboxylic acids and amines in aqueous PBS (pH 8, 40 °C), forming a peptide-bond amide without stoichiometric coupling reagents. The authors combined AI-guided mutation ranking with a FRET assay, reducing 7,999 in-silico variants at three active-site positions to five experimental candidates. The top triple mutant N155G/N218D/M222Q had reported relative activity of 753 ± 14% of wild type and also coupled biotin to a peptide fragment in water, extending beyond peptide–peptide ligation.

Technology: AI-guided enzyme mutation prediction combining binding-free-energy analysis of active-site substitutions with an experimental FRET-based rapid product-detection platform

This reduced the candidate set and enabled selection of the N155G/N218D/M222Q variant; the AI component was applied after the paper established the wild-type aqueous amidation reaction.
Test and result
The study reports that wild-type subtilisin BPN′ directly catalyzed condensation of free carboxylic acids and amines in aqueous PBS (pH 8, 40 °C), forming a peptide-bond amide without stoichiometric coupling reagents.
Limitation / still unknown
The reported chemistry is demonstrated for specific peptide fragments and a biotin–peptide coupling example under the stated aqueous conditions; the paper does not establish broad substrate generality or production-scale utility. The reaction requires follow-up for broader substrate scope and process optimization.

Technology: Algorithmic Iterative Reticular Synthesis (AIRES)

Editorial relevance 60 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
AIRES used probabilistic random-forest and Gaussian-process crystallization models to guide experiment selection across linker chemistries and reaction conditions. Its greedy and batch decision rules prioritized experiments predicted to yield distinct new crystals; automated synthesis, computer-vision crystal screening and subsequent single-crystal X-ray diffraction supplied experimental outcomes for model updates and structure determination. The AI-guided campaign found structures for 10 of 48 new linkers, with twice the distinct-crystal discovery rate of random exploration.
Test and result
AIRES combined probabilistic machine-learning predictions with robotic synthesis, optical crystal screening and single-crystal X-ray diffraction to explore zinc zeolitic imidazolate frameworks.
Limitation / still unknown
This is one paper-level experimental discovery campaign. The reported efficiency comparison is against a random-exploration baseline within the study, not an independent replication. Structures were identified by single-crystal X-ray diffraction; the paper describes discovery of ZIF crystals but does not establish application performance. The campaign covered a defined single-linker Zn-ZIF chemical and reaction space, not all reticular materials.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Across seven cohorts and five medical centers, targeted metabolomics confirmed six metabolites—imidazoleacetic acid, ergothioneine, N-acetyl-L-methionine, 2-keto-3-deoxy-D-gluconic acid, 1-methylnicotinamide and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate—as a panel for classifying rheumatoid arthritis against healthy controls and osteoarthritis. LASSO selected the six features, and logistic regression, random forest and XGBoost models were externally evaluated in geographically distinct cohorts; reported AUCs were 0.8375–0.9280 for RA versus healthy controls and 0.7340–0.8181 for RA versus osteoarthritis in three validation cohorts.

Editorial relevance 53 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Machine-learning feature selection narrowed targeted-validated metabolites to a six-analyte panel, and supervised classifiers combined the measurements to distinguish RA from healthy controls and osteoarthritis in multiple independent cohorts. Targeted mass spectrometry provided absolute quantification; the models produced the reported cross-cohort diagnostic discrimination.
Test and result
Across seven cohorts and five medical centers, targeted metabolomics confirmed six metabolites—imidazoleacetic acid, ergothioneine, N-acetyl-L-methionine, 2-keto-3-deoxy-D-gluconic acid, 1-methylnicotinamide and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate—as a panel for classifying rheumatoid arthritis against healthy controls and osteoarthritis.
Limitation / still unknown
This is a cross-sectional case–control diagnostic study, not prospective screening or evidence of improved patient outcomes. The authors note that disease activity and treatment effects were not assessed, so prognostic and treatment-monitoring uses are not established. Some mechanistic relevance of the six metabolites remains uncertain.

31 Oct 2025University of Science and Technology of China

Random forests capture cancer-specific variation in measured immune-cell response assays

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Random-forest models combined receptor–ligand expression measurements to estimate experimentally observed natural-killer-cell responses to tumor samples. Cancer-specific models generalized better within their studied cancer types than a pan-cancer model, whose separate-test AUC fell to 0.638. This is assay-level biological model validation, without established clinical treatment-selection benefit.

Technology: Random forests combining receptor–ligand expression features for assay-response classification

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Random forests learned nonlinear combinations of expression features linked to measured assay outcomes, enabling the observed distinction between cancer-specific and pan-cancer response prediction. Generic classifier benchmarks alone and untested clinical benefit are not the admitted claim.
Test and result
The source analyzed 76 distinct NK-cell samples against fourteen ovarian-cancer cell lines, then extended modeling across cancers. Random forests used 70:30 training/test partitions, ten-fold grid-search tuning and twenty random repetitions. A separate pan-cancer test set produced AUC 0.638 and accuracy 63.52%; source-reported breast- and gastric-cancer models reached separate-test AUCs 0.831 and 0.865. The result concerns measured assay response and its cancer-dependent generalization.
Limitation / still unknown
Random tumor–immune-cell pair partitions do not establish complete donor/cell-line independence; shared entities could affect apparent generalization. Upstream feature screening isolation and supplementary pair-level reconstruction were not verified. Five patient-derived AML samples and one treated patient do not establish prospective clinical efficacy or broad therapy-selection utility. Operational cell preparation, experimental manipulation and treatment protocols were not adjudicated.

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Learned aggregation of geometric/biomechanical simulation indicators produced a patient-specific risk category; clinicians retained decision responsibility.
Test and result
The commercial model combines about 50 engineered simulation indicators using machine learning. In 10 retrospective cases with at least 3 years of follow-up,6 had elevated risk and 4 developed type 1a endoleak;2 elevated-risk cases remained event-free. The additional 10 planned cases assessed clinician decisions; not all underwent the originally planned intervention, and follow-up was short.
Limitation / still unknown
Only 10 historical cases support the represented outcome comparison, with no controlled assessment of planning benefit. The learned algorithm architecture and training overlap are not detailed here. Prospective decisions changed treatment or prevented the planned intervention in some cases, so absence of an event cannot validate an untreated counterfactual. The planned cohort had only median 3 months follow-up and no target events.

Finding: In two multicenter cohorts totaling 597 people, LASSO feature selection and five machine-learning classifiers produced a six-metabolite plasma panel for gastric-cancer diagnosis, with AUCs of 0.947–0.982 in discovery and 0.920–0.951 in validation. The panel included isovalerylcarnitine (C5), which was lower in cancer plasma and paired tumor tissue; the paper further reported a Mendelian-randomization association and cell-assay evidence linking C5 treatment to reduced gastric-cancer cell migration and invasion through calpain-associated changes in VE-cadherin and MMP2.

The C5 mechanistic work was follow-up metabolomics, Mendelian-randomization, proteomic-correlation and in-vitro experimentation; the record does not imply that machine learning alone established the mechanism.
Test and result

Limitation / still unknown
The cohorts were case-control clinical samples and do not establish population-screening performance or improved patient outcomes. The 2024 IDDF abstract (DOI 10.1136/gutjnl-2024-IDDF.267) is an earlier disclosure of this same project, not a separate discovery. Source checked; independent replication not assessed.

The 82 confirmed hits were tested for single-dose activity against the sensitized E. coli ΔtolC screening strain; this is not evidence that all 82 work against wild-type bacteria or in infections. The 90-fold improvement refers to hit rate relative to the HTS training experiment. Some additional compounds were selected for dose-response testing; do not imply all virtual hits were validated. A publisher correction fixed a coauthor’s misspelled first name and did not change results.

AI contribution
Learned clinical-history embeddings and gradient boosting combined prior records, vital signs and laboratory values to estimate mortality risk; ordinary decision-curve analysis compared model outputs.
Test and result
The original preprint analyzed 2,161,689 encounters from 829,610 individuals after excluding encounters with major subsequent interventions, then reweighted the remaining sample. Hospital-grouped ten-fold evaluation reported XGB-EWS AUC .932 versus NEWS .902. The represented claim uses the October 14, 2025 preprint; the November 2026 journal abstract changes the cohort and numerical results, which are not assigned to the earlier date. Encounters from one person can recur and were treated as independent; hospital grouping does not establish patient separation across hospitals. Weighting depends on exchangeability and measured treatment predictors; unmeasured clinical factors can bias the hypothetical no-intervention estimate. Net benefit is a threshold-dependent weighted statistic, not a count of lives saved. Simulated staff-time savings and real-world implementation effects were not tested.

Researchers applied information-flow analysis to this AI-derived product and precipitation observations, then cross-checked the main spatial pattern using independent ERA5 reanalysis. The AI contribution is the neural-network-derived satellite soil-moisture product; the causal analysis is not itself an AI model. The spatial pattern was broadly checked with ERA5, while pathway attribution depends on ERA5-reanalysis variables and the assumptions/limitations of information-flow causal inference. Results concern boreal warm seasons and the analyzed 2003–2020 satellite period (ERA5 cross-check spans 1979–2021).

Prospective multicenter validation of TriVerity links a 29-mRNA host response to infection type and near-term severity

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: In the prospective SEPSIS-SHIELD study, a machine-learning blood test using isothermal amplification of 29 host-response mRNAs was evaluated in adults presenting to 22 emergency departments with suspected infection or sepsis. Among 1,222 patients with valid results, its bacterial and viral scores distinguished clinically adjudicated infection status with AUROCs of 0.83 and 0.91, respectively, and the system also produced a separate score for risk of ICU-level care within seven days. The test’s high/very-high and low/very-low interpretation bands had 92–99% sensitivities and specificities for selected infection/severity endpoints.

Technology: TriVerity on the Myrna instrument, using logistic-regression classifiers on expression measurements for 29 host-response mRNAs

Editorial relevance 60 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: prospective or independent check. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The locked machine-learning classifiers convert the amplified host-response mRNA profile into separate likelihood scores for bacterial infection, viral infection and need for critical-care interventions within seven days. The multicenter clinical study measured how those AI-generated scores performed against blinded physician adjudication and near-term clinical endpoints.
Test and result
In the prospective SEPSIS-SHIELD study, a machine-learning blood test using isothermal amplification of 29 host-response mRNAs was evaluated in adults presenting to 22 emergency departments with suspected infection or sepsis.
Limitation / still unknown
This is prospective diagnostic/prognostic validation of a specific host-response test, not discovery of a causal infection mechanism and not evidence that use of the score improves patient outcomes or antibiotic decisions. Of 1,441 enrolled patients, 1,222 had valid test results; the main diagnostic analysis used 729 consensus-adjudicated patients, and 1,120 were evaluable for prognosis. Clinical adjudication is not a perfect microbiological gold standard, and the study reports lower accuracy when uncertain adjudications are included. Performance and predictive values may vary with local infection prevalence and case mix. This is distinct from the earlier VB10 10-gene signature paper (DOI 10.1016/j.ebiom.2021.103352), which used different genes, cohorts and a different diagnostic score.

29 Sep 2025Zhejiang University; Harbin Genars Technology; GenVista Technology

Learned eleven-gene melanoma score associates with survival in public expression cohorts

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A penalized survival-model pipeline produced an eleven-gene melanoma score associated with observed survival in public expression cohorts. Model selection used both internal testing and an additional cohort, so the latter is not an untouched external test. The represented result is a retrospective prognostic association, without establishing novel cell types, causal tumor biology or improved treatment decisions.

Technology: Scissor phenotype-linked feature selection followed by LASSO Cox and ridge survival modeling

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Phenotype-linked selection and penalized learned survival modeling combined expression measurements into the represented score, enabling observed survival stratification beyond generic clustering or pathway enrichment.
Test and result
The source linked single-cell data to bulk survival data using Scissor, derived prognosis-related gene sets and compared seventy-two model combinations. It selected a LASSO Cox/ridge eleven-gene score using average performance across testing datasets. The paper reports a survival-group association in GSE65904, described as 215 samples, with modest time-dependent discrimination.
Limitation / still unknown
Outcome-informed upstream filtering and use of testing cohorts to choose the final model compromise independent validation. The paper reports 469 available TCGA records but a different final subgroup count in discussion, without a reconstructed participant flow here. Reported survival-time labels differ between text and figure captions, so exact time-specific AUCs are not adopted. Single-cell cluster labels, including the claimed MITF-positive T-cell population, were not independently authenticated as new biological cell types. Many individual genes already have melanoma associations. No causal mechanism, treatment benefit or clinical decision utility was demonstrated.

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
XGBoost learned residual prediction patterns and adjusted the prior pharmacokinetic estimates; comparison with measured subsequent concentrations supplies the specific clinical validation result. The pre-existing Bayesian model/dashboard alone is not treated as a new discovery.
Test and result
The source analyzed 292 successive-concentration pairs from 93 patients aged 2–22 years. XGBoost learned prediction errors using clinical features and prior drug measurements. Five-fold evaluation reported RMSE 3.78 ± 0.85 micrograms/mL versus 4.8 for Bayesian estimation alone. Absolute error improved modestly on average; the source also reports worsened predictions in a subset.
Limitation / still unknown
Multiple observations per patient were present, but explicit patient-grouped folds were not established in the reviewed Methods. Correlation-based feature selection and algorithm comparisons may affect internal performance; independent final evaluation was absent. Low concentrations below quantification were excluded. This is retrospective evaluation, without demonstrated clinical remission, safety improvement or validated continuous-learning deployment.

Fluorescence-polarization and NMR experiments supported direct binding, while disrupting the terminal binding motif abolished it; the preprint reported an affinity of 8.5 micromolar. Machine learning finds plasma protein signals up to 14 years before Parkinson diagnosis

The panel achieved test AUCs of 0.78 in incident and 0.795 in prevalent cases; nine selected proteins were already dysregulated 10–14 years before diagnosis. Editorial relevance 53 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Machine-learning classifiers were trained on UK Biobank plasma proteomic measurements to predict incident Parkinson disease; recursive feature elimination selected a 23-protein subset. The authors then tested the shared protein subset in the separate PPMI cohort using its own train/test split.
Test and result
Using UK Biobank measurements of 2,937 plasma proteins, researchers found 446 dysregulated proteins in incident Parkinson cases and used machine learning to select a 23-protein panel for prediction.
Limitation / still unknown
The result is a retrospective biomarker/prediction study, not a validated screening test or evidence that intervention based on the panel improves outcomes. The external PPMI analysis retrained and tested models in that cohort rather than evaluating a frozen UK Biobank model; validation AUCs varied by visit definition, and the reported maximum was 0.76. Protein associations and co-expression modules do not establish causal mechanisms. It is distinct from the earlier 2024 iRBD study in this ledger (DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-48961-3): separate cohorts and a different 23-protein/14-year result versus an eight-protein targeted panel and up-to-seven-year conversion finding; this record does not claim first discovery of presymptomatic plasma signals in Parkinson disease.

Machine-learning earthquake catalog reveals transform fault in the Zabargad Fracture Zone

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A 12-month network of ocean-bottom and land seismometers yielded a high-resolution catalog of more than 3,900 earthquakes in the northern Red Sea Zabargad Fracture Zone and Mabahiss Deep. The southern cluster’s diffuse seismicity and predominantly left-lateral strike-slip focal mechanisms reveal a NE–SW transform fault, which the authors describe as possibly in an early development stage. The northern cluster instead shows NW–SE normal-faulting lineaments related to extension.

Technology: OBSTransformer deep-learning phase picker, transfer-learned from EQTransformer and used through SeisBench

Editorial relevance 53 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The researchers compared EQTransformer, OBSTransformer and PickBlue for automatic earthquake detection and P/S phase picking on continuous ocean-bottom and land-station data. OBSTransformer was selected because it detected more events than EQTransformer while yielding fewer false detections than PickBlue and closer agreement with manual picks. The resulting detections and picks were manually checked and corrected, then used in the catalog from which the clusters and focal-mechanism analysis revealed the faulting pattern.
Test and result
A 12-month network of ocean-bottom and land seismometers yielded a high-resolution catalog of more than 3,900 earthquakes in the northern Red Sea Zabargad Fracture Zone and Mabahiss Deep.
Limitation / still unknown
The transform fault is inferred from the southern seismicity pattern and selected-event focal mechanisms, not directly imaged along its full geometry; the authors describe it as possibly in an early development stage. The catalog covers a 12-month deployment and is a snapshot that may not capture episodic ridge seismicity. Exact spreading-axis configuration remains uncertain. The earthquake-processing workflow was not fully automatic: investigators manually reviewed and corrected picks, removed events recorded by fewer than three stations, and used manual focal-mechanism analysis.

AI contribution
The supervised model selected a 540-CpG methylation signature from peripheral blood measurements to classify participants with and without brain insulin resistance, and the signature was assessed in two replication cohorts. The model-derived CpG set was then used for differential-methylation, gene-annotation and blood–brain correlation analyses.
Test and result
In the 167-person discovery cohort, the selected methylation signature was tested in two separate replication cohorts of 33 and 24 participants, with reported classification accuracy of 83–94%.
Limitation / still unknown
This is a biomarker-classification study, not a prospective clinical screening or intervention study. The discovery cohort had 167 participants and the replication cohorts were small (n=33 and n=24); replication accuracy is reported as 83–94%, and larger independent cohorts are needed to establish transportability. Blood–brain methylation correlations at 98 sites support a proxy relationship but do not show that peripheral methylation causes brain insulin resistance. The authors describe potential future diagnostic use rather than demonstrated clinical utility.

A liver-ultrasound classifier is evaluated in a South Indian community sample

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A study evaluated a neural ultrasound classifier using expert-agreed fatty-liver grades in a rural South Indian cohort. On a 66-person internal holdout, AUC was 0.90 for moderate-to-severe steatosis. Performance declined on an external dataset with a different reference and target; the result does not establish clinical outcomes or universal transfer.

Technology: ImageNet-pretrained InceptionResNetV2 convolutional neural network

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
A pretrained neural image model was fine-tuned on liver-ultrasound labels and generated participant-level probabilities from video-frame predictions.
Test and result
Of 261 expert-review candidates, 219 had usable scans and agreement by two blinded radiologists. Training, validation and test splits were at participant level, and image probabilities were averaged within each participant at test. The 66-person internal holdout contained 15 moderate-to-severe cases and yielded AUC .90 (CI .77–1.00). Without additional fine-tuning, an external 55-person biopsy-referenced dataset yielded AUC .76 (CI .64–.89) for any steatosis, a different target.
Limitation / still unknown
This record represents the original clinical analysis, not pooled performance of the accompanying systematic review. Selecting only radiologist-agreed cases removes difficult disagreements; initial inter-reader kappa was .44. Reference grades are visual ultrasound judgments, not biopsy confirmation for the community holdout. Different reported thresholds are optimized by Youden index, with independent threshold locking not established. External testing changes both outcome definition and reference, and subsequent fine-tuning uses that external population. No patient benefit, independent replication or broad population calibration is demonstrated.

The BDT combined kinematic and geometric variables, trained on simulated signal and data sidebands representing combinatorial background, and was used in the final candidate selection. Its output threshold was optimized together with particle-identification and Λ-veto criteria to maximize expected significance. This classifier contributed to background suppression; it was one component of the analysis, alongside upgraded trigger selections, detector reconstruction, and the statistical fit.
Test and result
Using 5.4 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton collision data collected in 2016–2018, LHCb observed 237 ± 16 Σ⁺ → pμ⁺μ⁻ decays and measured a branching fraction of (1.08 ± 0.17) × 10⁻⁸.
Limitation / still unknown
The paper reports an observation of the nonresonant rare decay, not evidence for the hypothetical intermediate X⁰ suggested by the earlier HyperCP candidates; no resonant dimuon structure is found. The retrospective cohort covered September 2020–March 2023 and was chronologically partitioned 70/15/15 for training, validation and testing. Finding: Applying PhaseNet-based phase picking to eight years of recordings from eight broadband stations, the study built a roughly 96,000-event Raton Basin catalog (local magnitudes −1 to 4.3) and resolved a previously unreported 2023 cluster with a Mw 4.3 event. Nearby wells had elevated injection volumes for about a year before the cluster; analysis of relocated events and 90 full centroid moment tensors also supports basement-rooted normal faults and possible elevated pore pressure. The authors interpret injection as a likely influence, not a demonstrated sole cause.

Technology: PhaseNet deep neural-network seismic phase picker in the LOC-FLOW workflow

Editorial relevance 47 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
PhaseNet picked P and S arrivals directly from continuous waveforms at eight broadband stations, including four stations not telemetered for routine cataloging. These picks enabled event association, relocation, and the expanded 2016–2024 catalog used to identify and analyze the 2023 cluster. PhaseNet enabled the denser earthquake observations; the injection comparison and full-CMT mechanism analysis were subsequent statistical and geophysical analyses.
Test and result
Applying PhaseNet-based phase picking to eight years of recordings from eight broadband stations, the study built a roughly 96,000-event Raton Basin catalog (local magnitudes −1 to 4.3) and resolved a previously unreported 2023 cluster with a Mw 4.3 event.
Limitation / still unknown
The authors report an association between nearby injection and seismicity and infer elevated pore pressure from positive isotropic components; this does not establish injection as the sole cause. They note possible residual isotropic-component artifacts from velocity heterogeneity or noise and explicitly limit interpretation of CLVD components. The paper gives slightly inconsistent catalog totals: 95,993 in the abstract and most text, but 95,933 in one discussion passage; this summary therefore says roughly 96,000. The newly resolved cluster is distinct from earlier Raton Basin seismicity studies cited by the authors.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A cross-spectral machine-learning model trained on 1,927 visible/UV photodetector records screened materials for extreme-ultraviolet response and selected α-MoO3 and ReS2 for device validation. At the Australian Synchrotron, the α-MoO3 detector showed measured responsivity of about 50–160 A/W depending on photon energy and bias (about 60–70 A/W near 13.5 nm); ReS2 reached about 20 A/W at 91.8 eV and 1 mV, close to the model estimate. The α-MoO3 device retained repeatable current response through 100 bias cycles under high-flux exposure.

Technology: Extremely Randomized Trees cross-spectral response prediction model

Editorial relevance 60 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The model learned relations between material/device descriptors and detector response across wavelength ranges from a 1,927-record dataset of visible and ultraviolet photoresponse measurements. It screened candidate materials for EUV responsivity and selected α-MoO3 and ReS2 for fabrication and synchrotron testing. The AI contribution was transferring response patterns across spectral domains to prioritize materials; experiments then measured the EUV detector performance.
Test and result
A cross-spectral machine-learning model trained on 1,927 visible/UV photodetector records screened materials for extreme-ultraviolet response and selected α-MoO3 and ReS2 for device validation.
Limitation / still unknown
The reported measurements are for the fabricated devices and stated synchrotron energies, biases and exposure conditions; they do not establish equivalent responsivity across all EUV wavelengths or device architectures. The paper reports α-MoO3 responsivity ranging about 50–160 A/W across test conditions, while near 13.5 nm it reports about 60–70 A/W; ReS2 was tested at a specified energy/bias. The authors' silicon comparison varies with the comparison conditions and metric (the abstract gives about 225-fold, while the device discussion reports up to about 800-fold); this record therefore states the direct responsivity measurements without treating either ratio as universal. The material screening result is a small experimental validation set, not an exhaustive search.

29 Jun 2025China Agricultural University; Mississippi State University

Neural-model optimization improves tested silver-carp oil extraction

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An ANN-guided search selected extraction conditions for silver-carp viscera oil, followed by physical confirmation. The measured yield was 79.44%, compared with 76.68% at a response-surface-selected setting. This is a small process-optimization experiment; separate encapsulation improvements were not shown to be AI-selected.

Technology: Multilayer perceptron with genetic-algorithm search over its learned response surface

Editorial relevance 40 chemistry Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
A learned nonlinear extraction-response model actively supplied the search objective for a newly tested process setting, rather than only fitting previously measured yields.
Test and result
The ANN learned from 17 response-surface-design experiments, with 70/15/15 training/test/validation allocation and a three-input, ten-hidden-node architecture selected through trials. Its learned response served as the genetic-search fitness function. The selected setting predicted 82.45% extraction; follow-up measurements yielded 79.44%, versus 76.68% for the response-surface setting, with source-reported significant difference.
Limitation / still unknown
Seventeen training-design runs produce very small evaluation subsets, and architecture choice by trial/error limits generalization claims. The physical optimized-setting measurement is distinct from the reported high fit correlation; its 79.44% yield is below the 82.45% prediction. The result concerns one byproduct/process system rather than universal extraction efficiency. Gelatin/coacervation optimization, capsule stability and simulated digestion are separate conventional downstream experiments, so they are not credited as additional AI-guided discoveries.

Active learning identifies 28 new DFT-validated pressure-induced phase transitions

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Across 13 active-learning cycles, a graph neural network screened phase pairs for pressure-induced transitions and selected cases for density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations. DFT confirmed 28 previously unreported transformations; 14 high-pressure phases were dynamically stable at transition pressure, including 10 also predicted dynamically stable at zero pressure. The study also identifies a previously unrecorded dynamically stable monoclinic P2₁/c phase of Cr₂O₃.

Editorial relevance 53 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

AI contribution
The GNN screened 7,677 phase pairs for consensus transition-pressure predictions. Active learning selected high-confidence pairs for DFT equation-of-state calculations, and the resulting DFT outcomes were added to training data for subsequent cycles. The AI search was the discovery and prioritization mechanism; DFT calculations supplied the physical verification of the transitions.
Test and result
Across 13 active-learning cycles, a graph neural network screened phase pairs for pressure-induced transitions and selected cases for density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations.
Limitation / still unknown
These are computational predictions corroborated by DFT, not experimentally synthesized or observed phases. Of 28 transitions, 14 high-pressure structures were dynamically stable at transition pressure; only 10 were also predicted stable at zero pressure. Two selected phase-pair calculations remained difficult to converge. The paper's discovery count excludes 18 rediscoveries, and individual stability remains subject to DFT approximations.

5 Jun 2025Johns Hopkins University; Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory; Gdansk University of Technology

Generative machine learning guides experimental synthesis of LiZn₂Pt and NiPt₂Ga Heusler phases

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Researchers combined a generative probabilistic crystal-graph model (PGCGM) with an ALIGNN stability predictor to propose and screen ternary structures, then used the model outputs to guide synthesis. They experimentally synthesized phase-pure LiZn₂Pt and NiPt₂Ga; the measured NiPt₂Ga adopts a tetragonal Heusler structure rather than the model’s cubic proposal, with DFT comparisons supporting its lower energy. They also synthesized LiZn₂Pd as a human-selected follow-up that was not among PGCGM’s candidate outputs. This is one paper-level AI-enabled synthesis workflow and three related compounds, not three separate records.

Technology: PGCGM generative Wasserstein GAN for ternary crystal structures; ALIGNN graph neural network for decomposition-enthalpy stability screening

Editorial relevance 53 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
PGCGM generated candidate crystal structures and ALIGNN screened their predicted stability. Researchers used these model outputs to down-select and choose Heusler-family candidates for synthesis. The authors note that expert judgment remained necessary and that LiZn₂Pt’s composition/structure appeared in the model training databases; NiPt₂Ga’s experimentally realized tetragonal structure was not the exact cubic structure proposed by PGCGM.
Test and result
Researchers combined a generative probabilistic crystal-graph model (PGCGM) with an ALIGNN stability predictor to propose and screen ternary structures, then used the model outputs to guide synthesis.
Limitation / still unknown
The reported synthesis outcome is experimentally characterized in the paper, but the AI was a candidate-generation and stability-screening aid rather than an autonomous discoverer: expert chemistry selected candidates and performed synthesis. LiZn₂Pt’s composition and Fm3̄m structure were already represented in Materials Project/OQMD training data, so its novelty is experimental realization rather than structure invention. The NiPt₂Ga experimental structure is tetragonal P4/mmm, differing from the cubic PGCGM proposal; the paper gives a DFT energy comparison. No superconductivity was observed, and magnetic ordering temperature for NiPt₂Ga was unresolved.

29 May 2025Northwestern University; California Institute of Technology; Stockholm University; Liverpool John Moores University; NSF-Simons AI Institute for the Sky; Zwicky Transient Facility collaboration

Autonomous BTSbot-nearby follow-up captures an infant supernova’s flash spectrum and constrains progenitor mass loss

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The BTSbot-nearby system used the BTSbot machine-learning classifier to identify SN 2024jlf in ZTF data and autonomously trigger a spectroscopic follow-up request, enabling spectroscopy about 0.7 days after first light. The early spectra showed short-lived Hα, He II and C IV flash-ionization features; comparison with two radiative-hydrodynamics model grids constrained the red-supergiant progenitor’s enhanced pre-explosion mass-loss rate to roughly 10⁻⁴–10⁻³ solar masses per year.

Technology: BTSbot machine-learning transient classifier integrated with the BTSbot-nearby autonomous follow-up program

Editorial relevance 53 astronomy Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
BTSbot identified the transient in ZTF alert data; host-distance and youth filters in BTSbot-nearby automatically triggered target-of-opportunity spectroscopy. This shortened latency to approximately seven minutes from alert-filter pass to first spectrum (spectroscopy was obtained about 0.7 days after first light), enabling observation of ephemeral flash features. Human and instrument teams obtained/interpreted observations; radiation-hydrodynamics models supported the mass-loss inference.
Test and result
The BTSbot-nearby system used the BTSbot machine-learning classifier to identify SN 2024jlf in ZTF data and autonomously trigger a spectroscopic follow-up request, enabling spectroscopy about 0.7 days after first light.
Limitation / still unknown
The AI contribution is event identification and automated prioritization, not inference of the stellar mass-loss physics. The rate is model-dependent and derived from two radiative-hydrodynamics code grids under adopted wind assumptions. The paper reports an individual nearby Type IIP event; this is not a population-level claim. The transient was originally reported to the Transient Name Server by a human observer, while the BTSbot-nearby program supplied rapid automated follow-up.

Editorial relevance 47 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
SISSO models learned compact descriptors of acid stability from existing calculations; model ensembles estimated prediction uncertainty, and a probability-of-feasibility acquisition strategy selected the next oxide for expensive DFT-HSE06 evaluation. The resulting feedback loop searched 1,470 candidates and identified 12 materials meeting the authors’ acid-stability criterion in 30 iterations, more efficiently than random selection.
Test and result
A SISSO symbolic-regression active-learning workflow identified 12 acid-stable oxide candidates from a pool of 1,470 within 30 active-learning iterations, using high-quality DFT-HSE06 Pourbaix calculations to evaluate oxygen-evolution stability.
Limitation / still unknown
This is a computational materials-property result, not experimental synthesis or electrochemical validation. The oxide structures were drawn from a known candidate space; the authors explicitly define “discovery” here as evaluating a previously unevaluated property, not discovering entirely new compounds. Acid stability is labeled at ΔG_Pourbaix^OER ≤ 0.10 eV/atom, a threshold that allows small positive values on the basis of potential self-passivation. The result depends on HSE06 DFT and the selected Pourbaix phases/conditions; practical catalytic stability must be tested experimentally.

Editorial relevance 53 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The team used LASSO to select a compact protein panel from the proteins associated with AD in discovery and replication analyses, then retrained logistic regression to predict clinical AD status. Limitation / still unknown
The cohort analysis is observational and does not establish that the associated proteins cause AD. The model’s clinical-status AUC was 0.72 in replication; performance was comparable to p-tau217 in the study’s comparison, but the reported AUC for frontotemporal dementia was also 0.73, limiting disease specificity. Orthogonal platform validation covered only subsets of the seven proteins (four proteins on Olink and two on Alamar), and the authors state that further work is needed before clinical use. The calculated free-energy maps at 500, 700 and 900 K show a smaller transition-state free-energy separation between terrace and step-edge regions at the two higher temperatures. Model energies and forces were compared with density functional theory on sampled configurations.
Limitation / still unknown
The spatial comparisons come from simulations of one nickel surface. The observed fit to reference energies and forces does not independently validate reaction rates, catalyst activity or the predicted temperature trend. The authors had already described qualitative terrace-site activation in a March 25, 2025 ACS meeting abstract; the May date refers to the journal spatial free-energy comparison.

Supervised decision tree among six ML classifiers uses five candidate predictors; the selected tree relies only on Barrett segment length.
Test and result
In 598 patients with follow-up through Jan 2024, 61 progressed within five years. The tree’s held-out test AUROC was .79; default sensitivity/specificity were 73.3%/70.4%, and a lower threshold yielded 93.3% sensitivity/58.5% specificity; segment-length thresholds define four risk groups.

The model was developed on 75% of a single-center veteran cohort and tested on a 25% held-out split (n=150); progressor pathology was independently verified by a second expert pathologist. Deep-learning seismic catalog reveals a potentially reactivated blind fault in Taiwan’s 2025 Dapu earthquake sequence

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A RED-PAN deep-learning phase picker enabled a catalog of 6,805 relocated events for the 11-day sequence following the M6.4 Dapu earthquake. Analysis of those events, focal mechanisms and velocity structure identified an east-dipping plane at about 5–10 km and a west-dipping plane at about 10–15 km; the authors infer the mainshock involved a previously unrecognized blind west-dipping fault and interactions with the known Muchiliao–Liuchia system. This is a localized structural interpretation, and the authors describe some fault associations as potential.

Technology: RED-PAN deep-learning seismic phase picker

Editorial relevance 47 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
RED-PAN detected P- and S-wave arrivals from continuous seismic recordings and supported event association and catalog construction; this catalog provided the relocated aftershock distribution used with focal mechanisms and velocity profiles to infer fault geometry. The fault interpretation itself involved human analysis, not an autonomous AI conclusion.
Test and result
A RED-PAN deep-learning phase picker enabled a catalog of 6,805 relocated events for the 11-day sequence following the M6.4 Dapu earthquake.
Limitation / still unknown
Peer-reviewed open-access short report. The principal west-dipping plane is interpreted as a potentially reactivated, previously unmapped blind fault; the paper calls some extended activity potential and recommends further monitoring. It is one earthquake sequence and the AI created the event catalog rather than independently deriving the tectonic model. A companion WTMA paper (DOI 10.1007/s44195-025-00095-9) analyzes the same Dapu sequence and similar two-plane geometry; it is a related, partly overlapping report and is not counted separately.

The work also found an ethyl–NHC product across tested reaction mixtures, suggesting additional catalyst-transformation pathways.

Technology: MEDUSA Search, an isotope-distribution-driven HRMS search engine with machine-learning ion-threshold regression and false-positive classification

Editorial relevance 60 chemistry Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Researchers generated candidate product-ion formulas from reaction fragments and catalysts; MEDUSA Search screened archived spectra using isotope-pattern matching, with two ML models estimating ion-presence thresholds and filtering likely false positives. It surfaced previously overlooked ions in old spectra; follow-up experiments with different NHC ligands and MS/MS tests checked the proposed vinyl–NHC products.
Test and result
MEDUSA Search mined archived high-resolution mass spectra and uncovered previously unreported vinyl–N-heterocyclic-carbene (NHC) coupling products in Pd/NHC-catalyzed Mizoroki–Heck reactions.
Limitation / still unknown
The claimed novelty is specific to vinyl–NHC coupling products in the studied Pd/NHC catalytic context. HRMS formulas alone cannot distinguish structural isomers, so the paper's MS/MS, ultrahigh-resolution measurements, reaction notebooks and independent experiments are essential evidence. The authors state that most other detected ions could not be associated confidently with reaction conditions because of incomplete metadata; those are not counted here.

A separate promoter-variant assay supported the four-base deletion, rather than a co-occurring 82-base deletion, as the key change associated with increased reporter activity.

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Deep-learning models predicted plant gene expression from regulatory DNA and used interpretability/occlusion and in-silico editing to identify promoter/5′UTR sequences likely to alter expression. The editing-plasticity predictions guided CRISPR-Cas9 targeting of ZmVTE4; the resulting four-base 5′UTR deletion was experimentally linked to increased gene expression and maize-kernel α-tocopherol. This is a measured crop-specific molecular/metabolite outcome, not merely an in-silico editing proposal.

A separate promoter-variant assay supported the four-base deletion, rather than a co-occurring 82-base deletion, as the key change associated with increased reporter activity.

The demonstrated editing result concerns one ZmVTE4 allele and maize material in the reported experiments; it does not establish effects on yield, nutritional outcomes in consumers, or performance across environments and genetic backgrounds. The paper reports limitations in prediction for rice and tomato and incomplete modeling of environmental influences; claims here are restricted to the maize ZmVTE4 test.

AI contribution
The locked MMAI score converted diagnostic biopsy images and clinical variables into patient-level prognostic scores. A previously developed multimodal AI score was retrospectively applied to archived diagnostic biopsies and follow-up from a prospectively collected Swedish prostatectomy cohort.
Limitation / still unknown
This is retrospective external prognostic validation using specimens and follow-up from a prospectively collected cohort; it is not prospective AI-guided care, a randomized test of biomarker-guided treatment, or evidence that using the score improves outcomes. Only 143 patients had evaluable images and complete covariates, and 88 were evaluable for adverse pathology; it is a single tertiary Swedish center. The model’s earlier development setting involved men receiving radiation in North America, so this tests transport to a different population/treatment context. A 2025 conference abstract describing this cohort is an earlier presentation of the same study, not another record.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: CHANCE, a supervised machine-learning model integrating patient-specific coding and non-coding mutations with drug and protein-interaction information, screened 5,197 TCGA/ICGC tumors against 923 FDA-approved non-oncology drugs. For ex-vivo validation, the investigators sequenced tumor cells from seven patients with pancreatic or esophageal cancer and tested CHANCE-prioritized drugs; at least one predicted non-oncology drug showed anticancer activity in tumor cells from five of the seven patients. This is patient-specific cell-assay validation, not a treatment-response study in patients.

Technology: CHANCE, a supervised gradient-boosted-tree model integrating coding/non-coding variants, protein–protein interaction networks, drug targets and drug-response data

Editorial relevance 60 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Trained on drug-sensitivity measurements from 318 cancer cell lines across 647 drugs, CHANCE maps each patient tumor’s whole-genome mutations to drug-target/pathway features and ranks non-oncology drugs by predicted patient-specific anticancer activity. Investigators used these predictions to select drugs for ex-vivo testing in tumor cells from seven patients; the reported five-patient activity result tests the model’s personalized prioritization.
Test and result
For ex-vivo validation, the investigators sequenced tumor cells from seven patients with pancreatic or esophageal cancer and tested CHANCE-prioritized drugs; at least one predicted non-oncology drug showed anticancer activity in tumor cells from five of the seven patients.
Limitation / still unknown
Only seven patient-derived samples were tested, from pancreatic or esophageal cancers; at least one prioritized non-oncology drug showed activity in five. This was an ex-vivo drug-sensitivity assay, not clinical treatment, and the study does not establish efficacy, safety, dosing or patient benefit. The 5,197-tumor/923-drug screen is computational prediction; only the small patient-derived subset had experimental validation. Drug-response predictions may include drugs represented in training, as the article notes 149 of 923 screened drugs were in the training data.

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Learned vessel segmenters generated lumen boundaries; an ensemble and downstream lesion analysis located and quantified lesions for comparison with manual QCA and cardiologist visual estimates.
Test and result
Retrospective three-center evaluation of 1,076 selected angiography images from 420 patients. Nine view-specific segmentation models combined DeepLabV3+/EfficientNet-B4, U-Net++/EfficientNet-B4 and U²-Net; training images from 2016 were separate from 2022 evaluation data. Against blinded manual QCA, the system detected 1,705/1,828 lesions (93%) versus 69% for visual estimation; on multiple-lesion images it identified all reference lesions in 86% versus 33%.
Limitation / still unknown
Manual QCA is the anatomical reference, not physiological significance or clinical outcomes. Selected frames excluded occlusions and poor-quality images; only reference lesions meeting size/stenosis criteria were counted. Lesion observations repeat within patients, and reported significance does not establish cluster-adjusted uncertainty. No prospective procedural or patient benefit was tested; training details in the supplementary material were not independently inspected.

Leveraging machine learning to uncover multi-pathogen infection dynamics across co-distributed frog families

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Among 1,281 sampled frogs, about 20% had at least one pathogen detected. Ranidae accounted for 74.3% of infections and had higher Bd intensity than the other two families. RF models identified host species and temperature-linked variables as key predictors; Bd/Rv infections were associated with higher latitudes and cooler, more stable temperatures, while Perkinsea trends differed. Three pathogens were screened/quantified by qPCR. RF models used overfitting checks, cross-validation and repeated 70/30 train/test splits (100 iterations); infection-status models covered up to 1,281 samples, with a 216-sample Bd intensity model. Results are observational and non-causal; the paper cautions about small positive groups/overfitting and does not sample across seasons.

16 Jan 2025California Institute of Technology; University of California, Berkeley; Elegen Corp

Active learning identifies a protoglobin variant with 99% yield and cis-selective cyclopropanation

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An iterative machine-learning campaign engineered the protoglobin from Pyrobaculum arsenaticum (ParPgb) for non-native cyclopropanation of 4-vinylanisole. After two model-guided rounds following an initial library screen, variant MPFDY gave 99% total cyclopropane yield and a 14:1 cis:trans ratio in the reported assay, compared with a parent variant that produced about 40% yield and favored trans product. The result demonstrates a specific sequence combination with improved yield and stereoselectivity in this enzyme scaffold.

Technology: ALDE (Active Learning-assisted Directed Evolution), using a bootstrapped deep-neural-network ensemble and Thompson sampling

Editorial relevance 47 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
ALDE trained on measured sequence–yield data, quantified model uncertainty, and selected variants across two iterative rounds in a five-residue, 3.2-million-sequence design space. Experimental screening measured product yield and stereoselectivity; the model-guided variants included MPFDY, whose combined mutations improved the targeted cis-product objective where tested single mutations and their naive recombinations did not.
Test and result
After two model-guided rounds following an initial library screen, variant MPFDY gave 99% total cyclopropane yield and a 14:1 cis:trans ratio in the reported assay, compared with a parent variant that produced about 40% yield and favored trans product.
Limitation / still unknown
Cyclopropanation is an established non-native enzyme reaction class; the study's distinct result is the ALDE-guided ParPgb sequence and its measured product yield/selectivity. The 99% yield and 14:1 ratio are study assay results, not evidence of industrial process readiness. The study is a single enzyme-engineering campaign.

15 Jan 2025BESIII Collaboration

Graph neural network enables first observation of Λc⁺ → ne⁺νe decay

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Using 4.5 fb⁻¹ of BESIII electron–positron collision data, the collaboration reports the first observation of the Cabibbo-suppressed Λc⁺ → ne⁺νe decay at greater than 10σ significance. It measures a branching fraction of (3.57 ± 0.34(stat) ± 0.14(syst)) × 10⁻³ and extracts |Vcd| = 0.208 ± 0.011(exp) ± 0.007(LQCD) ± 0.001(lifetime) for the first time from a charmed-baryon decay.

Technology: Graph neural network (GNN) trained on BESIII electromagnetic-calorimeter shower patterns

Editorial relevance 60 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The GNN separated neutron signal showers from the dominant Λc⁺ → Λe⁺νe background, whose neutron-plus-π⁰ calorimeter patterns are difficult to distinguish with conventional selection or boosted trees. The authors trained and calibrated it using large J/ψ control samples, then fitted its output distributions to extract the signal yield.
Test and result
Using 4.5 fb⁻¹ of BESIII electron–positron collision data, the collaboration reports the first observation of the Cabibbo-suppressed Λc⁺ → ne⁺νe decay at greater than 10σ significance.
Limitation / still unknown
The observation is an experimental result from the BESIII data sample; the branching-fraction and |Vcd| uncertainties include statistical, systematic, lattice-QCD and lifetime components as reported. The paper studies data-versus-simulation domain shift and network uncertainty; residual modeling differences contribute to systematic uncertainty. The |Vcd| extraction depends on lattice-QCD input.

Active learning guides experimental design of lead-free solder alloys

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Uncertainty-aware Gaussian-process models and multi-objective Bayesian acquisition guided seven design–experiment iterations. The study reports two selected alloys, Si-4 and Se-5, tested for tensile strength and fracture elongation. Reported averages follow the authors’ stated one-sigma selection of repeated tensile tests. Performance was mixed: the tested samples had poorer wettability and solder-joint shear strength than the commercial comparator. This is one laboratory alloy-design campaign, not evidence of industrial deployment or across-the-board superiority.

Limitation / still unknown
Averages follow a stated one-sigma selection of repeated tensile tests; wettability and joint shear strength were worse than the comparator. No industrial deployment or independent replication was established.

8 Jan 2025Columbia University; Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence; collaborating institutions

GET and interaction assays link a leukemia-risk PAX5 variant to stronger NR2C2 binding

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The General Expression Transformer (GET) model inferred cell-type-specific transcription-factor motif interactions from regulatory data and nominated a lymphocyte-specific interaction between PAX5 and nuclear-receptor-family factors. AlphaFold multimer modeling and PAX5 proximity-labeling in a B-ALL cell line supported interaction with NR2C2; the leukemia-associated PAX5 G183S variant showed increased PAX5–NR2C2 proximity signal. The variant-specific expression profile was enriched for predicted NR/3 and shared PAX5/NR/3 target genes, suggesting a possible regulatory mechanism for the germline risk variant.

Technology: GET (General Expression Transformer) foundation model for cell-type-specific regulatory grammar; AlphaFold2/AlphaFold Multimer for structural hypothesis assessment

Family AlphaFold: profile · models page

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
GET learned regulatory syntax across 213 cell types and used motif co-regulation to predict TF–TF interactions, which nominated PAX5/nuclear receptor family interactions in B cells. Structural modeling prioritized candidate binding interfaces. Researchers then used proximity labeling and mass spectrometry in a B-ALL cell line to compare wild-type PAX5 with the G183S leukemia-risk variant.
Test and result
The General Expression Transformer (GET) model inferred cell-type-specific transcription-factor motif interactions from regulatory data and nominated a lymphocyte-specific interaction between PAX5 and nuclear-receptor-family factors.
Limitation / still unknown
This is a cell-line interaction and expression analysis, not proof that the variant causes leukemia or directly alters disease risk through NR2C2. PAX5–NR2C2 interaction itself was consistent with prior evidence for the paralogue PAX2 and mouse pre-B cells; the specific reported distinction is increased interaction signal with PAX5 G183S and associated transcriptional enrichment. The authors call the disease-driving mechanism possible and identify limitations in cell-state and variant resolution.

8 Jan 2025European Space Agency (ESA), European Space Astronomy Centre

Machine-learning selection and Gaia astrometry confirm a 62-Jupiter-mass brown dwarf orbiting G 15-6

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A machine-learning search of Gaia DR3 two-body astrometric orbits flagged G 15-6 as a likely low-mass companion system. Combining Gaia’s astrometric orbit with archival radial-velocity measurements resolved the inclination ambiguity and yielded a companion mass of 62.43 (+6.16/−5.44) Jupiter masses, firmly in the brown-dwarf range. The authors identify it as the first independently validated brown-dwarf companion selected by their ML method. The radial-velocity data predate the study; the new result is the Gaia orbit and AI-guided identification that resolve the companion mass, not a newly observed companion in 2025.

Technology: Semi-supervised anomaly detection, extreme gradient boosting, and random-forest classifiers applied to Gaia DR3 astrometric-orbit solutions

Editorial relevance 47 astronomy Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The machine-learning pipeline ranked Gaia DR3 two-body systems for likely low-mass companions and selected G 15-6 as a brown-dwarf candidate. The Gaia astrometric orbit, combined with the independent archival radial-velocity orbit, resolved the inclination and established the companion’s mass; the models used only the Gaia orbital solutions for their candidate selection.
Test and result
A machine-learning search of Gaia DR3 two-body astrometric orbits flagged G 15-6 as a likely low-mass companion system.
Limitation / still unknown
The source study is an ML-assisted target-identification and Gaia-orbit analysis, not a 2025 direct detection. Archival radial-velocity observations already established binary motion but did not constrain the inclination enough to prove a substellar mass; Gaia astrometry supplies that missing orbital constraint. The wider candidate list includes false-positive Gaia solutions and unresolved stellar/substellar cases, which are not counted as confirmed companions here.

Deep learning enables multi-site bone marrow adiposity genetics in UK Biobank

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Deep learning measured bone marrow fat fraction at four skeletal sites in UK Biobank MRI data; after quality control, 48,608 participants contributed to genome-wide analyses. In the white-participant meta-GWAS, the study reported 67, 147, 134 and 174 independent significant variants for femoral head, total hip, femoral diaphysis and spine, mapping to 54, 90, 43 and 100 genes, respectively. Analyses also identified site- and sex-specific genetic associations and added signals in multi-ancestry analyses.

Editorial relevance 53 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The study applied deep-learning models to segment four skeletal regions and derive bone marrow fat-fraction phenotypes at UK Biobank scale. Those AI-derived measurements were the phenotypes used in the study's subsequent genetic association analyses; the paper's genetic findings are not themselves outputs of a generative model.
Test and result
Deep learning measured bone marrow fat fraction at four skeletal sites in UK Biobank MRI data; after quality control, 48,608 participants contributed to genome-wide analyses.
Limitation / still unknown
The GWAS, transcriptome-wide and colocalization results are statistical associations and candidate gene mappings, not proof of causal mechanisms. Ancestry subgroup sizes differ, and results do not establish clinical utility or disease prevention. The deep-learning measurement method was established in an earlier study; this record concerns the distinct population-scale phenotype and genetic findings. A 2025 author correction fixed a misspelling of AKNA as ANKA; it did not alter the reported analysis or findings.
